clue.text: Shout, but no longer make demands

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former, no longer so
to claim is to demand something as one's due

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out, having given up insisting on what they are owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a synonym for shouting.

clue.text: English minister — the constructive sort

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: An English clergyman who is a helpful kind of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructive' suggests helpful; literally it is one who builds or puts up.
explanation.definitionFit: One who erects or builds things is literally a constructor.

clue.text: Firm music-maker returning the crown

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: returning means the word for the singer is read backwards

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer who makes music

explanation.surface: A company musician brings back the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown worn by nobility, a lesser kind of royal headwear.

clue.text: Stay, having lots of time, in Alaska

parts.note: an anchor stays or holds a ship in place
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A long holiday spent in the far north of America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a location: the largest city in the US state of Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of the state, a port on Cook Inlet.

clue.text: The humblest faced accepting supplements

indicators.note: the word for faced takes in the other piece, holding it within

parts.note: to meet someone is to face them; past tense
to eke out is to supplement a scant supply

explanation.surface: The most modest person confronted a dose of vitamin pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekest is the superlative of meek, most humble and mild.

clue.text: Exhibitors of bathroom fittings

definitions.meaning: people who display or show things to others
fixed spray units for washing under, in a bathroom

explanation.surface: A trade fair stand displaying plumbing goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is people who show things; the second the familiar spray units over a bath or in a cubicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who show or display things are, literally, show-ers; a spray unit for washing in the bathroom is the other sense.

clue.text: No mean writer!

parts.note: someone far from stingy, freely parting with money, is also the surname of a twentieth-century English poet, Stephen

explanation.surface: Praise for a great author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No mean' sounds like praise for skill; read literally, it describes a person who is not mean with money, and the surname of the poet Stephen.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lays out money freely is not mean; Stephen of that name was a noted English poet.

clue.text: The last love game played

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of game are worked about, rearranged

explanation.surface: A final tennis match has been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love game' looks like a tennis term; love is O and game is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet, so the last of anything.

clue.text: A quarter got up about four, which is wearing

parts.note: E for east, one quarter of the compass

indicators.note: the word for got up surrounds four, placed within it

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone stood up at four and found it tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means tiring on the surface but is used as wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wears away gradually, as water does rock, is causing erosion.

clue.text: Vehicles left with some advantage on board

indicators.note: 'on board' means inside the ship, so the pieces go within the steamship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is on board
an edge is a slight advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: Cars departed, with a small lead over the rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledges are vehicles on runners for travel over snow.

clue.text: Complaint might ensue from a race he organised

indicators.note: the letters of 'a race he' are arranged afresh, put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a race he has set up could bring trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and pain in the ear is one such ailment.

clue.text: Observes a metal container is an unlovely thing

parts.note: to observe is to look at, to eye; third person form
ore is rock from which metal is extracted, so it holds metal

explanation.surface: Someone notices a metal tin that is ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a metal container' suggests a tin or can, but it is rock that contains metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensive to look at is an unattractive sight, the meaning of this compound word.

clue.text: Lie in the sun, then go to dance

parts.note: lying in the sun browns the skin, which is to tan

explanation.surface: Advice to sunbathe and then head off dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance of Argentine origin, an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Close around a listening device when winning

indicators.note: the word for close is placed so it surrounds the listening device

parts.note: the close of something is its finish or conclusion
the ear is the organ we hear with

explanation.surface: A bug planted while someone is victorious, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' suggests a bug; it is simply the body's hearing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning in the sense of charming: a winning smile is an attractive, lovable one.

clue.text: Withdraw touching and moralistic treatise

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on, as in a letter heading
a tract is a short pamphlet, often a religious or moral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes back a moving, preachy essay.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement is to withdraw it.

clue.text: Soldiers go ahead of newsmen to check

indicators.note: the soldiers come before the newsmen in the answer

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the press is the collective name for journalists

explanation.surface: Troops advance in front of reporters to hold them back.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to restrain or hold in, a synonym of check as a verb.

clue.text: Beat a friend hollow and scoffed

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pit is a hollow in the ground
to scoff is to eat greedily; past tense

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed a mate soundly and mocked him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat hollow' reads as thrash, and 'scoffed' as mocked; scoffed means ate greedily, and hollow is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the heart, to beat rapidly and irregularly, throb.

clue.text: Left about ten — and that's a bad sign

indicators.note: the word for left goes around ten, which sits within it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone departed around ten o'clock, which bodes ill.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen, especially one foretelling trouble, is a warning sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Sending letters to cause an RAF officer distress

parts.note: PO is a Pilot Officer in the RAF, the British air force
to sting is to hurt or upset

explanation.surface: Mailing letters to upset an air force officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Posting is mailing letters, dispatching them by post.

clue.text: Understand lies are being spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters of 'lies are' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that falsehoods are being circulated.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise is to grasp or become aware of a fact.

clue.text: To agree unreservedly

parts.note: accounts tally when they agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Agreeing wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely, without reservation.

clue.text: A miner's dog Rex

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed
R stands for Rex, the king, as on British coins

explanation.surface: A mineworker's pet dog is called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': A miner is dog plus Rex. R for Rex (Latin king) appears in royal ciphers such as GR.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal-mining worker; the word also names a coal-carrying ship.

clue.text: Cuts out cheats

definitions.meaning: carves or shapes with a bladed tool
swindles, an informal sense of the verb

explanation.surface: Someone removes swindlers from a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the carver's tool used as a verb; the other is slang for swindling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor carves shapes with a bladed tool; to swindle someone is the slang sense.

clue.text: Nice tax arrangement — but it's not right

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of 'Nice tax' puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasant tax deal, but something is off about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, so not correct in detail.

clue.text: The Italian queen turning to the first lady for help

indicators.note: both pieces together are read backwards, turned around

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
Eve, the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: An Italian queen turns to Eve for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IL plus ER to give RELI, to which EVE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to bring help or aid to someone in distress.

clue.text: Consumers may well be twisters!

parts.note: diners eating long pasta strands twist them round a fork, so the eater turns them

explanation.surface: Customers might turn out to be swindlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisters' suggests cheats or tornadoes; here it is what diners do with long pasta on a fork. The clue reads as the pasta being twisted by those consuming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin pasta strands are wound round a fork as they are eaten.

clue.text: An army holding unit is to move up

indicators.note: the word for army contains the letter for unit, holding it inside

parts.note: a host is a great army, a multitude
I, the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: A military force grips a unit and advances.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise or lift up.

clue.text: Perfect ladies endlessly making changes

indicators.note: the remaining letters are altered in order, rearranged
the final letter of the word ladies is cut off, leaving it without an end

explanation.surface: Flawless women who keep on altering things.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: A letter of introduction

definitions.meaning: the first letter of a name, as on a monogram

explanation.surface: A note recommending someone to a new acquaintance.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter of introduction is a known phrase; split, it gives the first letter of a name and an adjective meaning first or opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of a name is one sense; introductory, coming at the beginning, is the other.

clue.text: Come out in support of the man at executive level

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words 'the man at executive'

explanation.surface: Declaring backing for the boss at board level.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Much will appear dull going around at 50

indicators.note: the word for dull surrounds the other two pieces

parts.note: grey describes a dull, overcast day
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone warns that life will seem drab when they reach fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatly is an adverb of degree meaning a lot, to a large extent.

clue.text: Showing uncommon respect for the royal staff

indicators.note: uncommon means unusual, so the letters of respect take an unusual order

explanation.surface: Treating the palace employees with rare deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal staff' suggests palace servants; it is the rod a monarch holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental rod carried by a monarch as an emblem of sovereignty.
